from typing import Literal
import mas_operators as operator
from . import prompt as prompt_custom
from scripts.async_llm import create_llm_instance


from scripts.evaluator import DatasetType

class Workflow:
    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        llm_config,
        dataset: DatasetType,
        aggregator_llm_config=None,
    ) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.dataset = dataset
        self.llm = create_llm_instance(llm_config)
        self.aggregator_llm = create_llm_instance(aggregator_llm_config) if aggregator_llm_config else self.llm

    async def __call__(self, problem: str):
        star = operator.Star(worker_llm=self.llm, aggregator_llm=self.aggregator_llm, num_agents=3, worker_prompts=[prompt_custom.LIGHTUP_WORKER_ROWCOL, prompt_custom.LIGHTUP_WORKER_NUMBERED, prompt_custom.LIGHTUP_WORKER_COVERAGE], aggregator_prompt=prompt_custom.LIGHTUP_AGGREGATE_SELECT)
        draft = await star(problem)
        seq = operator.Sequential(llm=self.aggregator_llm, num_rounds=1, prompts=[prompt_custom.LIGHTUP_FINAL_FORMAT])
        solution = await seq(f"Problem:\n{problem}\n\nDraft answer:\n{draft['response']}")
        return solution["response"], {
            "worker": self.llm.get_usage_delta(),
            "aggregator": self.aggregator_llm.get_usage_delta(),
        }

Solve the Light Up puzzle below.

Focus on row/column visibility structure:
- Place bulbs only on empty cells.
- No two bulbs may see each other along a row or column unless blocked by a black cell.

Return a candidate bulb list only, inside a single triple-backtick code block.

```text
[(r, c), (r, c)]
```
If you think there is no solution, return:

Puzzle:
{problem}
"""

Use exactly this format:

If you think there is no solution, return:
